Invoke when column headers reliably indicate PII or credentials and the output CSV will leave the current trust boundary.","prompt":"Given a CSV whose output will be shared, published, or sent downstream, identify the column names or name patterns that must not be disclosed, then run qsv select with a single negated regex selector listing those identifiers (for example: qsv select '!/SSN|account_no|password/' input.csv). The negated selector retains every column that does not match and drops every column that does. Single-quote the selector so the shell does not expand or split it. After running, inspect the emitted header to confirm no matching column remains and that all expected non-sensitive columns are still present before handing the output to the next column reordering or inspection"],"intervention_moves":["Enumerate the sensitive column names or a regex pattern that matches them","Build a negated regex selector in the form !/pattern/ that matches only those sensitive names","Run qsv select with that selector on the input CSV","Verify the resulting header omits every matching column and preserves the remaining columns","Hand off the redacted CSV to the downstream sharing or export step"],"contraindications":["Sensitive columns are not known and cannot be pattern-matched","Data must retain all columns for internal analysis","Column names are misleading or absent","The sensitive data may live under innocuous column names that the regex cannot detect"],"triggers":["A CSV will be shared, published, or sent to a downstream system","Column headers contain known sensitive identifiers such as SSN, account_no, password, or similar PII/credential labels","A pattern can be written that matches the sensitive column names to be removed","A privacy or compliance review requires excluding named sensitive columns from the exported file"],"workflow_steps":["Identify the sensitive column names or a regex pattern that matches them, for example SSN, account_no, and password.","Construct a single negated regex selector that matches those names, such as !/SSN|account_no|password/.","Run qsv select with the negated selector against the input CSV, single-quoting the selector to protect it from shell interpretation.","Inspect the output header: confirm no column matching the sensitive regex remains, and confirm that expected non-sensitive columns are still present.","Proceed with sharing, publishing, or exporting the redacted CSV only after the header check passes."],"constraints":["The selector must be a negated regex (!/pattern/) so non-matching columns are retained and matching columns are dropped.","The regex is evaluated against column names, not cell values; it cannot detect sensitive content stored under unrelated headers.","The selector should be single-quoted when passed through a shell so the pipe characters and other special characters are not interpreted by the shell.","Verification of the emitted header is required before the output leaves the trust boundary.","This guardrail operates on column names; it must not be treated as a substitute for content-level inspection when headers are unreliable."],"cautions":["A negated regex drops only columns whose names match the pattern; misnamed, missing, or newly added sensitive columns will pass through unnoticed.","If the pattern is too confirm both exclusions and retentions.","This move reduces disclosure risk for known named columns but does not guarantee full de-identification of the dataset."],"output_contract":["A CSV whose
